# Incident Report — DESKTOP-H8ALZBV Malware Infection (2024-08-15)

## Evidence Reviewed
- `2024-08-15-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (18,189 frames, ~11.7 MB, ~32.7 minutes). No IDS/Suricata alert exports or other artifacts were present in the evidence directory — attribution below is behavioral, derived from traffic and an artifact recovered from the capture itself.

## Victim Host

| Field | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | **10.8.15.133** | Sole local host generating the malicious traffic; LAN is 10.8.15.0/24, gateway/DC at 10.8.15.4 |
| MAC | **00:1c:bf:03:54:82** | ARP (`arp.src.proto_ipv4==10.8.15.133`) and Ethernet source on all frames from this IP; matches the DHCP client MAC issued lease by 10.8.15.4 |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-H8ALZBV** | DHCP Option 12 hostname, NBNS name registration (`<00>`/`<20>`), Kerberos CNameString `DESKTOP-H8ALZBV$` |
| Domain/workgroup | LAFONTAINEBLEU | NBNS name `LAFONTAINEBLEU<00>` (Workstation/Redirector) |
| Logged-in user | **plucero** | Kerberos `CNameString` between 10.8.15.133 and the DC (10.8.15.4) |

## Malware Family

**Behavioral assessment: Latrodectus-style loader (also tracked as WailingCrab lineage).** No IDS signature was available to confirm this — attribution is **behavioral**, based on:

1. **Delivery chain** — fake-invoice phishing lure (`quote.checkfedexexp.com`) served a ZIP (`Invoice 876597035_003.zip`) containing an obfuscated JScript downloader (`Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js`).
2. **Staged payload retrieval via BITS** — shortly after, the host fetched a second-stage PE32+ DLL over HTTP using `User-Agent: Microsoft BITS/7.8` (i.e., `bitsadmin`/BITS job abuse, a technique this loader family is known for), from the same C2 IP that later served as the beacon endpoint.
3. **PE artifact recovered from the transfer** — the downloaded DLL contains the embedded debug path `E:\work\ooooooops\181\knock_v1.1.8\knock\bin64\knock.pdb` and exports `DllRegisterServer`/`DllRegisterServerEx`/`DllUnregisterServer`/`DllGetClassObject`, consistent with regsvr32/rundll32-style loader execution. The `knock`-named internal build path is a known artifact associated with this loader family.
4. **C2 beacon signature** — sustained HTTP GET/POST to `/` on a bare (unresolved-by-DNS) IP, encrypted payload smuggled in the `Cookie:` header, and a distinctively malformed `User-Agent: Mozilla / 5.0 (compatible; MSIE 6.0; Windows NT 5.1; SV1; .NET CLR 1.0.3705)` (note the stray space before the slash) — a fingerprint consistent with this family's check-in traffic, not a real browser.

The beacon ran continuously from ~T+196s to the end of the capture (~T+1962s, ~29 minutes), one request roughly every 5–7 seconds, with the C2 returning HTTP 400 to nearly all check-ins (server-side filtering/whitelisting behavior).

## Indicators of Compromise (grounded in this capture)

**C2 endpoint**
- `72.5.43.29:80` — staged the second-stage DLL and received the ongoing beacon (`tcp.stream` 134, 142–164+). Never resolved via DNS in this capture (hardcoded IP).

**Malicious domains**
- `quote.checkfedexexp.com` → 104.21.55.70, 172.67.170.159 — served the malicious ZIP.
- `business.checkfedexexp.com` → 172.67.170.159, 104.21.55.70 — queried in the same delivery window; part of the same lure infrastructure.

**Malicious URLs**
- `http://quote.checkfedexexp.com/managements?16553a25e45250a41fd5&endeds=MIGpq&JStx=59bf050d37df88a9-ade43358-eaa1220b-0571422b-0f33e6aa150e86bafd0ed4&Ld=9d7502d88d752a27b1d00587309184b5a215` — HTTP 200, `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="Invoice 876597035_003.zip"`, `Content-Type: application/octet-stream` (frame stream 112).
- `http://72.5.43.29/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` — BITS-fetched second-stage DLL (frame stream 134, HTTP 200, 159,232 bytes).

**Transferred files**
- `Invoice 876597035_003.zip` — delivered ZIP archive (Content-Disposition header, stream 112).
- `Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js` — obfuscated JScript downloader, filename recovered from the ZIP central directory inside that same HTTP response body.
- Second-stage DLL, SHA256: **`b7aec5f73d2a6bbd8cd920edb4760e2edadc98c3a45bf4fa994d47ca9cbd02f6`** (exported via tshark `--export-objects http`, confirmed PE32+ DLL x86-64, internal PDB `knock.pdb`).

## Benign Context (not indicators)
- Bing/MSN/Edge telemetry (`c.bing.com`, `assets.msn.com`, `browser.events.data.msn.com`, `sb.scorecardresearch.com`, etc.) — the victim was performing a normal web search (likely SEO-poisoned result leading to the lure) immediately before the `checkfedexexp.com` queries.
- Microsoft Delivery Optimization / Windows Update (`msedge.b.tlu.dl.delivery.mp.microsoft.com`), OCSP (`oneocsp.microsoft.com`), `www.msftconnecttest.com` connectivity check, `acroipm2.adobe.com` Adobe update check — normal OS/application background traffic.
- DHCP/NBNS/LDAP/Kerberos/SMB/DCERPC between 10.8.15.133 and 10.8.15.4 — normal AD-domain-joined workstation behavior (used here only to establish host/user identity).
- SSDP M-SEARCH broadcasts, mDNS, LLMNR — normal local network discovery noise.

## Incident Summary
The Windows workstation DESKTOP-H8ALZBV (10.8.15.133, MAC 00:1c:bf:03:54:82), logged in as user **plucero**, was infected after a web search led to a fake FedEx invoice page at `quote.checkfedexexp.com`, which delivered a ZIP containing an obfuscated JavaScript downloader. That script used Windows BITS to retrieve a second-stage DLL (SHA256 `b7aec5f73d2a6bbd8cd920edb4760e2edadc98c3a45bf4fa994d47ca9cbd02f6`, internal PDB name `knock.pdb`) from `72.5.43.29`, consistent with a Latrodectus-family loader. The host then beaconed continuously to `72.5.43.29:80` for the remainder of the capture, exchanging encrypted data via the HTTP `Cookie` header under a spoofed legacy Internet Explorer user agent.
